pl-l2d37c1-d1e108.summary: Reports many who think very differently: evil will and evil act are sins, in no way good, nor from God as author in any respect, since done without God.
claims: Evil acts are not from God at all.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e111.summary: Explains that 'without him was made nothing' means sin, called nothing not because evil action or will is not something, but because it separates men from true being and leads to non-being; those who withdraw from participation in the highest good, which alone truly is, are rightly said not to be.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e114.summary: Notes Augustine on John: sin is nothing, and men become nothing when they sin.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e118.summary: Reports their conclusion: sin is nothing because it distances from true being; evil will, action, and speech are sins as transgression and disobedience against God's law; they exist, but from man or the devil, not from God in any way.
claims: Evil acts exist but are from man or devil.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e121.summary: Reports that they restrict Augustine's 'all that is, insofar as it is, is good and from God' to natures or substances, meaning substances and what they have naturally, concreated, as the soul naturally has intellect, talent, and will; Augustine calls man a nature and an evil man an evil nature.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e126.summary: Reports that on this view neither evil nor good acts are natures or substances, as Augustine seems to indicate in the Retractationes, explaining that a statement in De vera religione concerned substances and natures, not good actions and sins; so actions, if evil, are sins and not from God.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e129.summary: Cites Augustine against the Pelagians: the devil's works, called vices, are acts, not things.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e132.summary: Cites further: every evil is not a nature but an act, accident from a defect of good; so God did not make it, since all he made is nature.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e135.summary: Cites further: all that is good by nature God made from nothing, not the devil.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e139.summary: Infers that some things exist that are not from God, by which men are evil.
claims: Some things are not from God.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e142.summary: Notes the other side grants this too, relying on Augustine's reading of Isa 5:20 as about the things by which men are evil; so some things make men evil.
claims: There are things by which men are evil.

pl-l2d37c1-d1e145.summary: Argues that what makes man worse is not from God, since by God's authorship man is not made worse (83 Questions); so God is not author of the things by which man is made worse, which are sins; hence Scripture testifies in many places that God is not author of evils, that is, sins.
claims: God is not author of sins.

pl-l2d37c1.summary: Presents the opposing view: evil will and evil act are sins and in no way good or from God, since done without God. Sin is 'nothing' (John 1:3) not because it is no act but because it separates from true being and leads to non-being. Augustine's 'all that is, insofar as it is, is good' applies only to natures or substances and what is concreated with them, like intellect and will in the soul; acts, good or evil, are not natures, as Augustine distinguishes in the Retractationes. Augustine says the devil's works, vices, are acts, not things; evil is not nature but an act, so God did not make it. Yet there are things by which men are evil (Augustine on Isa 5:20), and what makes man worse is not from God; so some things are not from God, namely sins.
claims: Some hold evil will and acts are in no way good or from God.
Sin is 'nothing' because it separates from true being, not because it is no act.
'All that is, insofar as it is, is good' applies to natures and substances only.
Acts, good or evil, are not natures or substances.
Some things by which men are evil are not from God.
